article_content: Servotech Power Systems announced plans to install 5,000 EV charging stations across India via its subsidiary Servotech EV Infra, which will operate as a Charge Point Operator (CPO). The company cited India's goal of achieving 30% electric vehicle adoption by 2030 as a key driver. A ₹300 crore investment will fund a manufacturing plant in Uttar Pradesh under the state's 2022 EV policy. Founder Raman Bhatia stated, 'This initiative aligns with our focus on supporting India's evolving EV infrastructure needs.'

article_content: House Speaker Nancy Pelosi led jubilant lawmakers and discharged service members in singing 'God Bless America' to mark the imminent repeal of the 'don't ask, don't tell' policy. President Barack Obama signed the repeal bill on December 22, 2010, fulfilling a campaign promise. The 1993 policy barred openly LGBTQ individuals from military service, resulting in over 14,000 discharges. Pelosi emphasized that ending the policy would strengthen the military by allowing LGBTQ members to serve openly. 'This repeal will make our country stronger,' she declared, prompting an emotional rendition of 'God Bless America' attended by Representative Barney Frank, one of the first openly gay Congress members. Representative Patrick Murphy shared a poignant email from a gay Army captain in Afghanistan who contemplated suicide due to the policy's isolation. The captain found hope in Murphy's advocacy. The repeal passed the Senate on December 18, 2010, after previous Republican blockades. Defense Secretary Robert Gates and Admiral Mike Mullen advocated for a phased implementation to avoid court-ordered abrupt changes. The Pentagon developed revised policies, followed by certifications from Obama, Gates, and Mullen confirming readiness. A 60-day waiting period preceded the repeal's full enactment.
translated_content: قادت رئيسة مجلس النواب نانسي بيلوسي احتفالاً تاريخياً بإلغاء سياسة 'لا تسأل لا تُخبر'، حيث غنى المشاركون من تشريعيين وعسكريين سابقين 'ليبارك الله أمريكا'. وقع الرئيس أوباما القانون في 22 ديسمبر 2010، منهياً سياسةً استمرت 27 عاماً منعت المثليين من الخدمة العلنية بالجيش. شددت بيلوسي على أن الإلغاء 'يعزز قوة الجيش عبر احتواء جميع الأمريكيين الراغبين في الخدمة'. وصف النائب بارني فرانك، أحد أول المثليين علناً بالكونغرس، الحدث بأنه 'انتصار للكرامة الإنسانية'. روى النائب باتريك ميرفي قصة نقيب مثلي في أفغانستان كاد ينهي حياته بسبب العزلة التي فرضتها السياسة، قائلاً: 'قراءة أخبار جهود ميرفو منحني الأمل'. صادق مجلس الشيوخ على الإلغاء في 18 ديسمبر 2010 بعد معارضة جمهورية سابقة. طالب وزير الدفاع روبرت غيتس والأدميرال مايك مولين بتنفيذ تدريجي لتجنب إلغاء مفاجئ عبر المحاكم. تبع ذلك تطوير البنتاغون لسياسات جديدة، ومصادقة القيادات على جاهزية الجيش، ثم فترة انتظار 60 يوماً لسريان الإلغاء.

article_content: By Janet Tappin Coelho in Rio de Janeiro. A Brazilian man posted a Facebook message announcing plans to kill his wife over suspected infidelity. Franque do Nascimento Santos, 50, stabbed his 23-year-old wife Juliana Moreira de Melo three times in the neck at their Senador Camará home in west Rio de Janeiro on June 1. Hours earlier, he apologized to their two-year-old son in a post stating: 'Son, daddy loves you. Mummy cheated and must pay – she will die today.' Friends expressed horror in comments, with one asking: 'What have you done?' Santos surrendered to police the next day. Friends revealed they initially thought the post was a hoax. The victim's cousin Mayara Vinicius Melo, 18, disputed the infidelity claims, stating Juliana had expressed fear about Santos' recent behavior and temporarily left home before returning for their son. Witnesses reported tension at their final public appearance. The child now lives with his maternal grandmother, who told him his mother 'became a star.'
